value.answer: For most adults, short-term use at low doses looks safe, and that's what the health sites back up. Long-term is less clear. A preliminary abstract from the American Heart Association, presented in November 2025, linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to more heart failure. It hasn't been peer-reviewed and can't prove melatonin caused it, and some experts think poor sleep could be behind it. Sources also disagree on how long counts as short-term and on the right dose, and melatonin can interact with other meds, so check with a doctor or pharmacist before starting, especially if you have ongoing sleep trouble.
